answer: A market can require each agent to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may post bids, then slash that stake when a bonded counterparty proves fraud through signed transaction records. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply influence for free: every account needs its own stake, and each can lose it. A gale of fabricated profiles therefore ties up real capital at the wharf, while a beacon of public audit records helps honest traders identify repeat offenders.
